subject: silver fox
title: What If You Bred Only the Friendliest Foxes? Siberia Has Since 1959

scenes.text: What if you bred only the friendliest foxes? In Siberia, they started to look like dogs.
1959, Novosibirsk. Geneticist Dmitri Belyaev starts an experiment with silver foxes and one rule.
Each generation, only the tamest foxes get to breed, about one in ten. Nothing else is selected.
Within six generations, foxes are licking hands, whining when people leave, and wagging their tails.
Then, in under a decade, come changes nobody chose. Floppy ears. Curly tails. Patchy coats. Shorter, rounder snouts.
By generation fifteen, their stress hormones had fallen by about half. The experiment is still running. Select for friendliness alone, and the rest of a pet seems to come with it.

description:
What if you bred foxes for friendliness and nothing else? Dmitri Belyaev began exactly that in 1959 at the Institute of Cytology and Genetics in Novosibirsk, and Lyudmila Trut has led it since his death in 1985.
Only the tamest foxes, roughly the top 10 percent, were bred. Within six generations some licked hands, whined and wagged their tails. Within a decade floppy ears, curly tails, mottled fur and shorter snouts appeared, and by generation 15 stress-hormone levels were about half those of wild foxes.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Nobody selected for floppy ears or curly tails. They just arrived with the tameness. Which animal would you tame next?
